_note: One unit = one lesson path in five steps. Write 'God' (the Muslim view shows 'Allah'). Verses by ref only (shown from src/data/ayahs.json); hadith by id only (shown from src/data/hadith.json). 'about' lines are our own words, never a translation.

intro.muslim: God gave Sulayman a kingdom like no other: the wind obeyed him, and he understood the speech of birds. One day, marching through a valley, he heard a tiny ant warning the others. Watch what he did.
intro.curious: Sulayman, known in the Bible as Solomon, was given a kingdom like no other: the wind obeyed him, and he understood the speech of birds. One day, marching through a valley, he heard a tiny ant warning the others. Watch what he did.

muslim.situation: You just got a new phone. A day later, your friend shows off a newer, better one.

options.label: Feel your phone is suddenly not good enough.
options.feedback: Very common. The Prophet ﷺ gave advice for exactly this feeling, and you'll see it soon.

options.label: Say alhamdulillah for yours, and be happy for your friend.
options.feedback: That's gratitude: seeing what you've been given, not what you're missing.

options.label: Start saving for theirs straight away.
options.feedback: There'll always be a newer one. The teaching shows a way off that treadmill.

options.label: Say nothing, but feel a bit jealous.
options.feedback: Honest. Gratitude grows with practice, starting with naming what you already have.

quran.about: Sulayman smiles at the ant's words and prays to be enabled to be grateful for the favour God gave him and his parents.
If you are grateful, God will give you more.
If you tried to count God's blessings, you could never number them.
Whoever is grateful is grateful for their own good.
Few of God's servants are truly grateful.

hadith.about: A believer's life is good either way: thankful in ease, patient in hardship.
Look at those who have less than you, so you don't belittle what you have.
Thanking people is part of thanking God.

insights.text: Gratitude has three parts: knowing in the heart that a blessing is from God, saying it with the tongue (alhamdulillah), and using the blessing in ways that please Him. Sulayman, the richest of kings, asked God to help him be grateful (27:19).
Looking at those with less, not more (Muslim 2963), is a simple habit that guards a heart against envy.

check.q: What did the ant say when Sulayman's army came?
options: Ants, go into your homes, or Sulayman and his soldiers may crush you without knowing
check.why: She warned the others to go home, so they wouldn't be crushed without the army knowing (27:18).

check.q: What did Sulayman do when he heard the ant?
options: He smiled and thanked God for His favour
He changed his route in anger
check.why: He smiled, and prayed to be grateful for God's favour (27:19).

check.q: What does God promise the grateful in 14:7?
check.why: If you are grateful, I will surely increase you.

check.q: Which way should you look, according to the hadith, to stay grateful?
check.why: Look at those below you, so you don't belittle God's blessings on you.

check.q: What does the hadith say about thanking people?
options: Whoever doesn't thank people hasn't thanked God
check.why: Whoever does not thank people has not thanked God.

reflection.muslim: Write down three things you were given today that you didn't earn. Thank God for each, and thank one person too.
reflection.curious: List three things you have that you didn't earn. Who could you thank for one of them today?
